PM.name: Self-Initiated Problem-Solving
PM.description: The CV names at least one specific, costly problem the candidate noticed on their own — not a task handed to them — and describes the specific action they took to fix it, without waiting for approval.
PM.anchor_5: Names a specific unassigned problem AND a specific self-built action taken to fix it.
PM.anchor_3: Describes initiative, but it's inside a task/project already assigned to them, or the "problem" is described only generically (e.g. "improved efficiency") without a named trigger.
PM.anchor_1: All bullets describe executing tasks that were already defined for them; no instance of the candidate identifying a problem before being asked to solve it.

PM.name: Spread Beyond the Individual
PM.description: The candidate points to a concrete, stated fact (a number, a timeframe, a named outcome) showing that what they built was picked up and used by other people — not just their own output.
PM.anchor_5: A specific, verifiable fact shows adoption by others (a headcount, "became standard," a named team/account using it, a retained process).
PM.anchor_3: Adoption is claimed but vague ("well received," "helped the team") with no concrete fact attached, or is limited to one or two named colleagues.
PM.anchor_1: Every initiative stays confined to the candidate's own metrics; no one else is mentioned as adopting or relying on the result.

PM.name: Ownership Through a Failure or Crisis Moment
PM.description: The CV describes a specific moment something went wrong or was ambiguous (an outage, a vendor surprise, a lost deal, a compliance risk), shows the candidate personally absorbed or resolved it — ideally before someone else felt the impact — and shows they wrote down or shared what happened afterward.
PM.anchor_5: Names a specific failure/crisis moment, the candidate's own resolution of it, and a follow-up artifact or shared lesson (a post-mortem, a documented root cause, a retained process change).
PM.anchor_3: Describes handling a difficult or ambiguous situation, but there is no unplanned failure/crisis named, or no evidence the lesson was written down or shared with anyone else.
PM.anchor_1: CV describes only steady, planned execution toward targets; no unplanned difficulty of any kind is mentioned.

PM.name: Direct Contact with the People Doing the Operational Work
PM.description: The candidate uses specific, concrete language about sitting with or coordinating directly with the actual people executing operational work (named roles — e.g. port officials, frontline account handlers, field engineers) rather than generic references to "stakeholders" or "cross-functional teams."
PM.anchor_5: Names a specific operational role or frontline group they worked alongside directly, with a concrete instance (not a recurring meeting cadence alone).
PM.anchor_3: Mentions cross-functional collaboration, but only in abstract organisational terms (presenting to leadership, "working with engineering and design").
PM.anchor_1: No operational, customer-facing, or frontline contact is described anywhere in the CV.

SPM.name: Self-Initiated Problem-Solving
SPM.description: The CV shows a pattern — two or more instances across their career, not one anecdote — of independently identifying unassigned, costly problems and building the fix themselves, at increasing scope or stakes over time.
SPM.anchor_5: Two or more distinct, specific instances, with visibly increasing scope/stakes across them (e.g. team-level, then account-level, then company-level).
SPM.anchor_3: Exactly one clear instance, or multiple instances at the same, unchanging scale.
SPM.anchor_1: At most one instance, and only within a narrowly assigned task — same bar as PM score 1.

SPM.name: Spread Beyond the Individual, at Scale
SPM.description: The self-built solution became the standard for an entire team, function, or company — not a subset of colleagues — with a durable outcome, and the CV shows the candidate drove that adoption themselves rather than it happening incidentally.
SPM.anchor_5: Adoption is company/function-wide, durable (still in use months+ later, or "core"/"standard"), and explicitly attributed to the candidate's own effort to spread it.
SPM.anchor_3: Adoption is real but limited to a subset of colleagues, a short time window, or the candidate's role in driving the spread (vs. it happening on its own) is unclear.
SPM.anchor_1: Same as PM score 1 — no evidence anyone besides the candidate used or relied on what they built.

SPM.name: Independent Ownership Through a Failure or Crisis Moment
SPM.description: The candidate resolved a high-stakes, ambiguous situation entirely on their own judgment — no mention of escalating to a manager or waiting for direction — and explicitly documented the lesson in a form other people could use afterward.
SPM.anchor_5: Explicit "no escalation" / solo-judgment language (or clear equivalent) AND a written artifact (post-mortem, SOP, shared write-up) resulting from it.
SPM.anchor_3: A crisis/failure moment is described and resolved by the candidate, but either the independence (no escalation) or the written follow-up is missing, not both.
SPM.anchor_1: No such moment is described, or it was handled via an established process/playbook already in place rather than the candidate's own judgment call.

SPM.name: Direct Contact with the People Doing the Operational Work
SPM.description: Sustained, repeated, specific engagement with frontline operational people over time — not a single visit or one-off interaction — or genuine domain fluency from having done the operational job themselves before this role.
SPM.anchor_5: Repeated/ongoing operational contact over time (multiple named instances, or prior hands-on experience actually doing the operational job).
SPM.anchor_3: One clear but isolated instance of direct operational contact.
SPM.anchor_1: No operational contact described, or it is only secondhand (relayed through someone else's research/interviews).
